newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Vicious short squeeze sees Aussie leap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Vicious short squeeze sees Aussie leap.

text.p: *AUD up a cent after a blistering rally came from nowhere as U.S. banks and funds were squeezed out of short positions
*Stop loss buying was triggered at 74 cents, $0.7420 and $0.7460 clearing out a lot of shorts and taking AUD to 3-wk high
*Break of $0.7440 improved chart position and analysts look to buy dips now. Building approvals data should not trouble
By 8.15 am (2200 GMT) the local currency was up at US$0.7450/55 having reached as high as US$0.7505 at one stage from US$0.7370/75 late here Tuesday.
The break of last week's peak of US$0.7440 had improved the chart outlook, although analysts would have been even more bullish if it had managed a NY close above US$0.7475 as well.

They doubted a sober local market would follow through on the rally and looked for a lapse to US$0.7440, but were encouraged enough to recommend buying dips for a rise toward major resistance at US$0.7550. A breach of US$0.7420 would the bounce was a false dawn and return the A$ to range trading.

Along with noteable Swiss bank bids overnight, dealers reported a large buy order for AUD/CAD worth around A$450 million from a Canadian corporate which was rumoured to be linked to the takeover of an Australian mining company.
The A$ was certainly stronger on the Canadian currency, being up at C$1.0314/25 from 1.0179/90 late here Tuesday.

It also got a boost from a bounce in US$/yen which carried the U.S. dollar above 118.00 for the first time since mid-May. The A$ followed, and again benefited from heavy short covering when 87.30 broke, to reach 88.09/19 yen from 86.58/68, its highest start in almost two months.

Traders said there was some suggestion the rally was due to fading speculation of a rate cut but most felt this was well wide of the mark, noting bill futures still had a 0.5 point easing priced in. The rise in the dollar actually made it easier for the Reserve Bank by lifting some of the currency risk.
Today's data on building approvals for June should confirm a an on-going recovery in the housing market but would have to be exceptionally strong to altermakret thinking on rates.
Median forecasts favour a fall of 1.5 percent following a 2.2 percent rise in May.
